newsitem.title: USA: Safeguards under US Treasury bank reform proposal.
newsitem.headline: Safeguards under US Treasury bank reform proposal.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury outlined the following capital protections and other safeguards as part of its financial modernization proposal unveiled Wednesday.
It said the following safeguards would apply if a bank holding company or a subsidary of a bank engaged as principal in activities not permissible for a national bank to engage in directly:
-- The bank would have to remain "well capitalized," in the highest regulatory capital category, exceeding normal requirements.

-- The bank would have to deduct from its regulatory capital the entire amount of its equity investment in any subsidiary engaged in such activities. This would ensure the bank would still be well-capitalized even if the envestment were a total loss.
-- The bank would have to be well-managed.
-- Any company controlling the bank would have to undertake that if the bank's capital fell below the well-capitlized level, it would be promptly restored.

-- Existing limits on loans and other transactions between banks and affiliated companies would be extended to bank subsidiaries engaged in such activities. Thus any transactions between the bank and the subsidiary would have to be conducted at arm's length, could not exceed 10 percent of the bank's capital, and would have to be fully collateralized. In addition, the bank's transactions with all affiliates, including the subsidiary, could not exceed 20 percent of the bank's capital.
-- Banks could not be held vicariously liable for obligations of a subsidiary or other affiliate that the bank had not assumed.
-- Bank reulators would be specifically required to assure that banks observed principles of corporate separateness.

-- Under the alternative that would allow some mixing of banking with commercial firms, banks would be prohibited from extend any credit to, or for the benefit of, any nonfinancial affiliate. (The other alternative would not permit nonfinancial affiliates.)
